infrastructure: Bulgaria has relatively fast urban internet speeds driven by competitive ISP market, though rural connectivity lags.
Sofia is developing a small data centre market.
5G deployment began in 2022, with urban coverage expanding.
talent: Sofia Tech Park and Technical University of Sofia are developing AI research capacity.
Bulgaria has a growing software outsourcing industry, creating applied AI development skills.
One of the EU's most severe brain drain problems, with population declining significantly since 2000.
governance: Bulgaria has struggled with corruption, ranking among the EU's lowest on governance indicators.
GDPR is formally in place; the Commission for Personal Data Protection is the regulator.
Recent political instability (multiple elections in 2021–2023) has hampered consistent AI policy development.
investment: EU structural funds are the dominant source of digital transformation investment.
Some international outsourcing companies have established development centres in Sofia.
Domestic AI startup investment is minimal.
economic_readiness: One of the EU's lowest GDP per capita nations, constraining enterprise AI spending capacity.
Growing IT services export sector is building digital economy foundations.
High poverty rates and digital divide limit broad-based AI adoption.
